Subject: Capacity vs feature split — decision & rollback playbook

Hi Marta,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — really appreciated the time. I pulled together two concrete packaging options for your platform team to evaluate: one focused on reserved capacity (throughput-first) and one focused on modular feature bundles (feature-first). I attached a short spreadsheet that shows cost delta, token economics, and suggested upgrade/downgrade triggers for each plan.

Quick summary:
- Option A — Reserved throughput pool: predictable latency, good for high-concurrency inference, higher base commit but lower per-token after threshold.
- Option B — Modular feature bundles: lower commit, pay-for-what-you-use for premium features (KV caching, priority routing), easier to prune features during slow periods.

Key question from your side: whether you want a single canonical plan with stepdown thresholds or an explicit two-path offering (we call this a capacity-vs-feature "splay"). Both routes have fallback/rollback mechanics but different commercial trade-offs.

If helpful, we can propose a conservative concession for initial pilot (one month free burst or 10% onboarding credit) and lock a rollback checklist so procurement can sign off quickly. Attached: CyanHealth_MRPM_v1.xlsx (cost math) and a one-page rollback-checklist.md.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm the preferred path (capacity-first vs feature-first) by EOD tomorrow.
2) If you pick feature-first, indicate which 3 features must be guaranteed in pilot.
3) If procurement needs the rollback language, I can loop legal and provide a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Thanks — I’ll hold time for a quick call if you want to walk the sheet together.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Team — forwarding Cyan Health thread. Marta asked for a one-paragraph rollback process and procurement wants minimal amendment language. Thoughts on the recommended concession and which features we should lock for a feature-first pilot?

Notes/context:
- Cyan runs both burst and steady; they value predictability but want to avoid a big up-front commit.
- I was thinking: offer a 6-week pilot, 10% onboarding credit, and a trigger-based rollback (detailed below). If we do feature-first, lock: KV cache hot-keys, priority routing for 2 endpoints, and model quantization profile (no surprise perf regressions).

Proposed rollback paragraph (first stab):
"In the event that production performance or cost materially deviates from the agreed thresholds during the pilot, Redwood Inference will (a) immediately revert Cyan Health to the prior model/configuration within 24 hours, (b) provide a full token-cost credit for the pilot period proportionate to the measured overage, and (c) deliver a data snapshot and post-mortem within 5 business days. Approval for rollback requires sign-off from Cyan Health Head of AI Ops and Redwood Director of Customer Success or their designees."

Please reply with edits — trying to keep procurement happy while not over-committing the platform team.

Thanks,
Camila

Camila / team —

Thanks for the draft. A few practical edits from an infra + support perspective:

- Reversion SLA: 24 hours is reasonable for config toggles; for full model rollback that requires KV cache invalidation and warmup, call it 48 hours. We should split the clause: config revert (24h) vs model variant revert (48h).
- Credit calculus: rather than "full token-cost credit," tie credits to "measured delta vs baseline forecast" to avoid open-ended exposure. Example language: "a token-cost credit equal to the measured delta between agreed forecast and actual usage during the pilot period, capped at 30% of the pilot invoice."
- Approval path: require Head of AI Ops + Redwood Director of Customer Success OR automated trigger (3 consecutive SLA misses within a 24h window). That gives engineering an automated way to protect the customer without manual delay.

I also recommend we offer the following commercial bridge to make feature-first palatable: 2 weeks of free burst capacity (up to X tokens) plus a one-time 10% onboarding credit. That keeps initial revenue impact bounded.

I'll attach a short rollback-checklist.md that lists steps for engineering ops.

Ben Carter
